darkmatriarch
children.text: please keep sharing this stuff every chance you get. Personally I expect the web as we know it to be unusable in early 2027 if nothing changes.

What strategy? The current strategy is like the strategy of a rocket sled.

Everyone compete with each other to compete with China to get a brass ring that's entirely unknown.

It's development at breakneck speed and blinders on for the sake of development (also known as IPO)

There are technical uses and there are social uses. The latter are by design echo chambers and often destructive of independent thinking and physically destructive as in "You are immortal, now go step in front of automobiles" (and this is fact, not fiction)

The difference between this and the development of the atomic bomb, which it eerily parallels, is that scientists assured themselves prior to its construction that it would not destroy the entire world in a chain reaction. That is not the case here.

I previously posted [1]

quote

I just listened to a video linked here [0] in which key points are that AI is reaching a point where it can be truly dangerous as in "overthrow the government" and that we need to nonetheless race development because CHINA is racing development, and YET, the more advanced our models are, the more advantageous it is for China (or others) to simply steal it.

So, in defending against an "enemy" we are also doing their work for them. Nice. We have been down this path before, but maybe this is more dangerous than nukes. Maybe not.

AND that security from leakage within AI companies, while extremely crucial, is secret and therefore unknown.

Given the value of the inside information, it could rival past government espionage scandals, and its status is completely known.

This all seems to boil down to security issues, and the very deliberate weakening of cyber defenses, along with incompetent political hacks in charge, and the sudden arrival of powerful vulnerability detection and exploitation, could take it all down in 2017 if not sooner, even without outside attack.

[0] https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50522546

end quote

source.text:
I don't know, maybe it's just me.

Does it feel to you like we're boiling the oceans in a desperate attempt to build something "smarter than human?"

Do you notice that the idea that "AI will cure cancer" is predicated on the belief that we've found the data that will lead to a cure and us humans just somehow missed it?

Are you also watching your former boss, who laid you off for AI, slowly turn the nail gun that is AI automation towards his own face?

Are you also currently avoiding plane flights at all costs?

Personally, I like AI a lot, but I think conversational language models were a mistake. Isn't this the root of AI psychosis for most? Isn't autocomplete turned conversational just sycophancy for our delusions even if we have guardrails in place?

Don't you think that if you can't explain the functionality of an AI model that means you probably shouldn't use it?

If you said yes to any of the above I'd love to hear your thoughts on the current state of things. Please, vent your heart out.

If you said no to everything please just be quiet, this will be fun for the rest of us.
source.title: Ask HN: Should we shut down current AI strategy? Vent Your Heart Out
